Writes the XRDB artwork patterns into your AIOMetadata profile. Your AIOM credentials go directly to your chosen instance.

XRDB caches the artwork it renders, in memory and on disk, under a one-way digest of the title, the image type and the look. Cached artwork is kept for up to 72 hours by default and is rendered again when next requested.
XRDB can also run on your own machine, with your own API keys and no shared rate limits.
XRDB has no user accounts. It does not ask for your name or email address, sets no cookies, and runs no analytics or advertising.
XRDB only reads from Trakt: the movies you have watched and the movies you have paused part-way through. It never writes to your Trakt account, so it adds no history, check-ins, ratings or lists.

XRDB serves its own addon, so Stremio can use this profile without AIOMetadata. It supplies metadata for a title you open and no catalogue rows of its own, so rows and your library keep the posters their own source supplied. AIOMetadata above serves the rows itself, which is what puts badges on them, along with logos, episode thumbnails and full metadata.

XRDB sits in front of your media library and re-renders artwork — posters, backdrops, thumbnails and logos — with overlays: ratings, quality badges, genre and age labels, a trending tag, and aggregate or score-based presentations. You design a look once in the configurator and every image your setup requests is rendered to match.
XRDB stores the access and refresh tokens Trakt issues with the profile, encrypted with AES-256-GCM. They are never included in the profile’s settings, an export, or any response from XRDB.
XRDB uses Trakt but is not endorsed or certified by Trakt.
